set.body:
FIRST SLICE DONE, and the answer is smaller than the surface suggested - which is what chief hoped
when they refused to scope this as "probe 422 types".

SCOPE, per chief: start from what is reachable in PUBLISHED RECEIPTS. The align codec serialises
these enums: AlignState, Contradiction, CostTerm, Exclusion, ExternalState, Facet, FidelityMode,
SourceNodeRef. Of those, only three have PARAMETERISED cases at all:

  AlignState.Source(ref: SourceNodeRef)
  AlignState.Distorted(ref: SourceNodeRef, facets: NonEmptySet[Facet])
  AlignState.External(state: ExternalState)
  FidelityMode.Distorted(facets: NonEmptySet[Facet])
  SourceNodeRef.Situation(id: SituationId)
  SourceNodeRef.Segment(id: SegmentId)

JUDGEMENT: NONE OF THEM CARRIES AN INTRINSIC INVARIANT THAT CONSTRUCTION ALONE VIOLATES. Their
invariants are one of two kinds, and both are already held elsewhere:

  DELEGATED TO THE FIELD TYPE. `facets: NonEmptySet[Facet]` cannot be empty because NonEmptySet
  cannot be empty - cats holds it, not the enum case. `Situation(id)` and `Segment(id)` take opaque
  ids with their own constructors. There is no cross-field relation among the parameters.

  RELATIONAL TO A CONTEXT, NOT TO THE VALUE. `Source(ref)` can name a node that is not in the view -
  but that is a claim about a view, not about the value, and the system already answers it as a
  runtime exclusion rather than a type error: `CostBreakdown.unreachable` exists precisely for "the
  candidate reference is not a node of the view". Sealing the case would not make the pair
  (state, view) coherent; only checking against a view does.

So the receipt-reachable enum surface needs NO sealing work. That is a real result rather than an
absence of effort: the reason the enum door is dangerous in general is that it admits a value whose
FIELDS ARE JOINTLY UNLAWFUL, and none of these has fields that can be jointly unlawful.

THE ONE REAL INSTANCE IS OUTSIDE THIS SCOPE. ExclusionCause.BelowMembership(threshold: Double)
carries an intrinsic invariant - finite and in [0,1] - and construction violated it: collab blocked a
candidate of mine this morning because PlacementResolution.of accepted BelowMembership(NaN),
+/-Infinity, -0.1 and 1.1 and published each as the rule in force. It is NOT receipt-reachable:
PlacementResolution appears in no codec. So the first slice's boundary excludes the only member with
a demonstrated defect, and whoever does slice two should start there rather than repeat this one.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not enumerate the parameterised enum cases outside the align receipt. Two
attempts at a census earlier today gave 1325 and 827, both wrong, and I published neither. The
population size is still unmeasured and the next slice needs a method rather than a grep.

METHOD NOTE for whoever takes slice two: the test is not "is this case parameterised" but "can its
parameters be JOINTLY unlawful". A single opaque-typed parameter almost never can; two or more
parameters with a relation between them almost always can. BelowMembership is the interesting
counter-example - ONE parameter, and unlawful on its own because the lawful set is a subrange rather
than a type.
set.title: align: which parameterised enum cases carry an invariant construction could violate - judgement pass over the receipt-reachable surface
